original_question: Find explicit parametrizations or another complete description of all rational solutions to the Diophantine equations y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1, y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1, and y^2 - x^2 y + z^2 + 1 = 0.
target_in_paper: Section 3 ("Describing all integer/rational solutions"), specifically the paragraph stating that, for rational solutions, the smallest open cases are equations (3), (4), and (5), together with the immediately stated equivalence to the homogeneous integer equations (6), (7), and (8).
correct_elements: The draft already isolates the exact three affine equations targeted by the paper for the rational-solution problem, and it correctly asks for a full description of rational solutions rather than just asking whether rational points exist.
missing_details: The three equations are to be treated separately, not as one simultaneous system.
The primary ambient domain is Q: one is asking for all triples (x,y,z) of rational numbers, with no positivity, coprimality, or integrality assumptions in the affine formulation.
In the paper, the task is not restricted to giving a single explicit parametrization; any complete and satisfactory description of all rational solutions is in scope.
To make the question fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, it is helpful to record the paper's explicit equivalent homogenized reformulation in integers.
Homogeneity is not part of the original affine question; it enters only through the equivalent homogeneous cubic reformulation stated by the paper.
refined_question:
Treating the equations separately, determine the complete set of rational solutions (x,y,z) in Q^3 to each of the following affine equations:
1) y^2 + z^2 = x^3 + 1,
2) y^2 + z^2 = x^3 - 1,
3) y^2 - x^2 y + z^2 + 1 = 0.
An acceptable resolution should give a complete explicit description of every rational point on each surface; it need not consist of a single parametrization, but it must account for all rational solutions.
equivalent_formulation: As stated in Section 3, this is equivalent to solving in integers the homogenized cubic equations y^2 t + z^2 t = x^3 + t^3, y^2 t + z^2 t = x^3 - t^3, and y^2 t - x^2 y + z^2 t + t^3 = 0.
justification: The nearest paper formulation is not a conjecture or theorem but the Section 3 classification statement about the smallest open equations for describing rational solutions. Your draft is very close because it names exactly the three affine equations singled out there. The main adjustment is scope: the paper allows any complete description of the rational solution sets, whereas your draft foregrounds parametrization as if that were required. The paper also immediately records the homogeneous integer reformulation, so including that as the sole alternate version makes the question more self-contained while staying faithful to the original intent.
